meta.principle: Prestige proves curiosity and judgment, not permanent combat superiority. All endings award the same prestige.

arcs.name: The Unlisted Ward
arcs.motivation: Edda needs an independent field witness because official corrections require evidence and she refuses to publish refugees' addresses.
arcs.era: Present-day reconstruction after the Great Schism; not evidence of who caused the Great Severance.
arcs.site: Two chairs face an empty doorway. Only the smaller chair has fresh repairs. Household numbers continue across a wall that modern surveys label vacant.
arcs.monster_lore: A failing municipal automaton denies entry according to a damaged census index. Its shield and rust armor are ordinary surviving technology, not proof of ancient sentience.

quests.title: A Chair for Someone Missing
quests.premise: A repaired chair stands outside a household listed as empty. Edda wants a name restored without revealing where the family now sleeps.
quests.opening: The chair isn't abandoned. Someone fixed its leg yesterday. My register says nobody lives here. Help me find which record is lying.
clues: The small chair has fresh binding; the large one has weathered dust.
A torn census slip retains an occupancy mark but loses its address line.
The doorplate carries a household number, not a military unit number.
quests.answer: The household was relocated, not erased by death; occupancy and present address are separate records.
choices: Restore the name, withhold the address
Aid workers need Edda as an intermediary
The public index gains a name without a location.
Share a sealed address with relief workers
The family must trust a restricted channel
A confidential aid entry accompanies the corrected name.
Let the family authorize the correction
Recognition waits for consent
Edda leaves an unsigned entry for its owner to approve.
quests.completion: One blank line is a person again. That is enough for today.
quests.reward_lore: A repaired doorplate, returned with permission. An empty address is not an empty life.

quests.title: The Number Beneath the Number
quests.premise: Two surveys disagree about the same doorway. The older mark describes a utility district, while the newer mark counts households.
quests.opening: I can make both columns agree by throwing one away. That would be neat. It would also be wrong.
clues: The lower numeral is cut into stone; the upper numeral is painted.
The lower series skips occupied doors but follows conduit junctions.
The cabinet labels the two columns district and household.
quests.answer: The records use different counting units. Neither number alone proves a missing family.
choices: Publish both systems with a legend
Readers must learn a harder index
Both numbering schemes remain visible.
Prioritize the household number
Maintenance crews need an extra lookup
Residents gain a readable primary label.
Prioritize the utility number
Civil claims need an attached note
Repair crews recover the older route.
quests.completion: Two numbers. One door. Now the next clerk won't have to invent a disappearance.
quests.reward_lore: Two legitimate marks preserved on one seal. Agreement is not the same as accuracy.

quests.title: An Obedient Lock
quests.premise: The Ward Indexer repeatedly bars a relief passage because its stale register has no authorized households.
quests.opening: It follows the register exactly. That's the problem. Stop it without calling the people behind that door intruders.
clues: The automaton's authorization plate names a municipal service.
Its rejection stamp predates the relocation notice.
Its patrol follows the same blocked doorway, never the occupied side lanes.
quests.answer: A stale authorization list, not a new Concordium order, causes the obstruction.
choices: Submit the fault to municipal repair
Formal repair takes time
The obstruction is recorded as a service failure.
Mark a community-managed passage
Residents bear responsibility for access
A local maintenance notice replaces the rejection stamp.
Keep the old index as evidence
Storage and custody cost effort
Edda retains a copy before a technician repairs it.
quests.completion: The machine can be replaced. The excuse that nobody was there cannot.
quests.reward_lore: A retired municipal key, preserved as evidence of a failed register rather than a trophy taken from a resident.

quests.title: The Route Kept Inside
quests.premise: A relocation notice hides a relief route inside its fold. Publishing it would help aid crews and expose people who chose anonymity.
quests.opening: The fold kept this dry. It also kept it private. Don't mistake finding a route for owning the people at its end.
clues: The exterior bears a public household mark.
The interior names a relief transfer, not a military movement.
The notice says restricted delivery, with no claim of faction disloyalty.
quests.answer: The hidden line protects recipients; it is not proof of a clandestine faction transfer.
choices: Copy destinations only to relief staff
Aid depends on a trusted custodian
A restricted relief list is prepared.
Publish quantities without destinations
Delivery requires another channel
A public needs report excludes identifying details.
Return the notice to its household
Verification stays local
The record owner decides what may circulate.
quests.completion: You brought back the paper. More importantly, you didn't bring back a list of targets.
quests.reward_lore: A ribbon used to refold a notice. Information can remain useful without becoming public.

quests.title: The Right to Remain Unlisted
quests.premise: The ward can be recognized without every resident being named. Edda asks how to preserve that distinction for the next census.
quests.opening: I wanted to fill every blank. Now I know some blanks are chosen. Help me write a register that can tell the difference.
clues: The doorplate proves occupation, not identity.
The two numbering systems serve different public needs.
The folded route shows that privacy and assistance can coexist.
quests.answer: A register needs a consent category; anonymity must not be treated as abandonment.
choices: Create an anonymous occupied category
Named claims still require witnesses
The ward is recorded without listing every person.
Keep a sealed identity supplement
Trust rests with its custodians
Public and restricted records are separated.
Require renewed household consent
Records become slower to update
Residents retain a recurring say in their entry.
quests.completion: The ward has a place on the map. Its people still have a choice about the register.
quests.reward_lore: A ring engraved with a doorway and no name. Recognition without possession.

arcs.name: The Hollow Muster
arcs.voice: Hear the gap. Metal tells on itself.
arcs.motivation: Tovan repairs signal bells for civilians who worked beside Iron and Legion crews. He needs an outsider to compare records neither employer will share with him.
arcs.era: A recent evacuation; does not rewrite either faction's founding or the Great Schism.
arcs.site: A muster bell hangs over boots facing away from the parade line. A second rope leads into a workshop, not a command tower.
arcs.monster_lore: A derelict construct scavenges the same signal cable each time workers repair it. Its repeated damage explains the missing bell beat without implicating a faction commander.

quests.title: The Missing Fourth Beat
quests.premise: A four-beat muster signal sounds only three times. A scorch mark could indicate sabotage or an ordinary failure.
quests.opening: Three beats call a shift. Four clear the yard. Listen before you accuse someone of desertion.
clues: The tally labels the fourth beat evacuate.
A missing cable reaches the workshop, not the barracks.
Boots point toward an exit rather than the parade ground.
quests.answer: The interrupted signal is an evacuation instruction, not an incomplete pledge.
choices: Restore the evacuation signal first
Production waits while crews test it
Workers hear a full warning sequence.
Post a visual warning alongside repairs
Someone must maintain the signs
A second warning channel is established.
Use a staffed manual bell
A worker must remain on watch
The warning no longer depends on one cable.
quests.completion: Four beats. No speech. That will do.
quests.reward_lore: A discarded bell clapper. Its worth lies in the warning people finally heard.

quests.title: Boots Facing Outward
quests.premise: A roll marks a crew absent, but their boots and tool tags suggest an organized civilian evacuation.
quests.opening: An empty parade line doesn't tell you where they went. Look at the wear on the soles.
clues: Boot soles carry workshop grit, not barracks polish.
Tool tags follow a work roster, not a military rank.
The roll records departure after the evacuation beat.
quests.answer: Civilian crews left under a safety instruction; absence from muster is not evidence of military desertion.
choices: Correct the work roster publicly
Employers must acknowledge the mistake
Civilian absences become documented evacuations.
Attach witness statements privately
Public suspicion may persist longer
Workers gain a restricted proof of departure.
Let the crew speak collectively
The crew must spend time organizing
The roll carries their own account.
quests.completion: Boots don't swear oaths. People do. Keep the columns separate.
quests.reward_lore: A civilian tool tag whose owner left through the proper safety exit.

quests.title: What Keeps Taking the Cable
quests.premise: Every repaired bell cable disappears. Tovan needs the malfunctioning wrecker stopped before anyone can rely on the signal.
quests.opening: Same length missing. Same bite in the copper. Someone calls it sabotage; I call it a repair that hasn't found its cause.
clues: Cable ends show mechanical shearing, not a clean hand cut.
The wrecker's cargo cradle contains matching wire.
Its salvage route loops through the bell support.
quests.answer: A derelict salvage routine repeatedly removes the cable; this evidence cannot identify a human saboteur.
choices: Document the mechanical cause
A politically useful accusation loses force
Tovan files a repair failure, not a faction charge.
Invite both crews to inspect it
Inspection delays reopening
Rival crews share a witnessed fault report.
Retain the damaged cable as proof
The workshop must store it
The physical evidence survives the repair.
quests.completion: It can break once. It doesn't get to break the same warning forever.
quests.reward_lore: A sheared cable ferrule kept to teach future repair crews what the failure looked like.

quests.title: The Shift Neither Banner Claimed
quests.premise: The evacuation roll includes workers supplied by two rival institutions. A single-banner memorial would erase half the crew.
quests.opening: They held the same rope. Their employers can argue about the brass plaque after I finish the names.
clues: The roll interleaves two supply stamps.
All entries share one shift and one exit record.
A margin note identifies the common bell crew, not a new faction.
quests.answer: This was a practical shared work shift, not evidence that Iron and Legion secretly merged.
choices: List names without institutional marks
The sponsors lose visible credit
The memorial centers the workers.
Keep both supply stamps
Visitors may read politics into the plaque
Both contributions remain documented.
Place separate plaques beside one bell
The shared work is less immediately obvious
Each institution keeps its record at a common site.
quests.completion: One rope. Enough hands. Don't make the metal say more than that.
quests.reward_lore: A work token stamped by two suppliers. Cooperation on one shift does not erase their disagreement.

quests.title: A Warning Is Not an Oath
quests.premise: The repaired bell can become a ceremonial monument or a working civilian warning. Tovan cannot maintain both roles without help.
quests.opening: A monument rings when someone important visits. A warning rings when someone ordinary is in danger. Which job are we paying for?
clues: The fourth beat has a specific safety meaning.
The absent crew obeyed it.
The wrecker fault explains why the warning failed.
quests.answer: Preserving memory requires an accountable maintenance plan, not merely a new ceremonial label.
choices: Keep it a working warning bell
A crew must fund regular checks
The yard retains its evacuation signal.
Move the original into a memorial
A replacement must carry the warning
The original becomes evidence beside a working copy.
Give maintenance to a joint work council
Rival crews must keep cooperating
The bell gains shared civilian custodians.
quests.completion: If it rings and people get home, remember whoever kept it working.
quests.reward_lore: A loop braided from retired bell rope. It honors maintenance, not a borrowed military oath.

arcs.name: The Zero Berth
arcs.voice: Read the unit before you buy the number.
arcs.motivation: Sella needs a field examiner outside her former OmniCorp employer and Meridian creditors to distinguish damaged cargo from a manipulated claim.
arcs.era: A present-day dispute over storage fees; no claim about the founding of either faction.
arcs.site: A berth marked zero contains a crate with an inward-facing shipping stencil. A polished scale shows the same value even with no cargo.
arcs.monster_lore: A local fee collector uses disputed storage claims to bar inspection. Their crimes are individual acts, not proof that every Meridian trader or OmniCorp employee colludes.

quests.title: The Weight of Nothing
quests.premise: A manifest prices an apparently empty crate. Sella suspects the buyer purchased storage space, not goods.
quests.opening: Empty doesn't mean free. It also doesn't mean fraud. Show me what the contract actually sold.
clues: The cargo column is blank, not marked lost.
The billed unit is berth-day, not mass.
The empty scale retains its tare reading.
quests.answer: The base contract sells reserved storage time. An empty crate alone does not prove stolen cargo.
choices: Disclose the storage unit prominently
The broker loses an easy sales shorthand
Future buyers see what is being sold.
Offer a partial refund for ambiguity
The seller bears a negotiation cost
The buyer receives compensation without a fraud finding.
Keep the contract and add an explanation
The buyer still pays its stated fee
The annex records a clarified but unchanged agreement.
quests.completion: Now we can argue about a real price instead of an imaginary shipment.
quests.reward_lore: A tare weight marked zero cargo. It distinguishes a valid storage fee from an invented shipment.

quests.title: The Label Facing Inward
quests.premise: An inward stencil makes a returnable container look like a new delivery. Its direction matters more than its serial number.
quests.opening: Serial's genuine. Story's facing the wrong way. Turn your attention, not the number.
clues: The stencil faces the crate interior.
The scale log marks outbound packaging as returnable.
The repeated serial refers to the container, not two cargo loads.
quests.answer: The crate is a returned container. A repeated container serial is not proof of duplicated cargo.
choices: Correct the delivery count
The carrier's volume claim shrinks
The record separates container returns from goods.
Flag the stencil for physical inspection
A shipment waits at the berth
An inspector confirms direction before settlement.
Publish a return-label standard
Dock crews must relabel stock
A clearer standard prevents the same dispute.
quests.completion: A number can be honest while the headline above it isn't.
quests.reward_lore: A shipping seal from a returned container; its orientation explains its record.

quests.title: The Fee at the Evidence Door
quests.premise: An extortionist blocks examination of the disputed invoices. Sella needs access, not a verdict about the whole port.
quests.opening: They charge to let me inspect the fee they charge. Stop that little circle. Leave the innocent crews out of it.
clues: The demanded fee is absent from the signed contract.
The collector bars only the inspection door.
The invoice identifies a private collector, not a faction decree.
quests.answer: The obstruction is an unauthorized inspection fee; the original storage contract remains a separate question.
choices: File the unauthorized fee with witnesses
Witnesses must risk being identified
The collector's obstruction becomes a documented claim.
Protect the witnesses' identities
The case needs a trusted intermediary
Sella submits a restricted statement.
Send the physical invoices to neutral custody
Settlement is delayed by transport
A neutral examiner receives the originals.
quests.completion: Access restored. Verdict still open. I like it when those are separate sentences.
quests.reward_lore: A fee seal invalidated for unauthorized use. A collector's misconduct is not a judgment on an entire port.

quests.title: Rent Inside Rent
quests.premise: A valid storage contract has been billed twice by nesting an already paid container-day charge inside berth rent.
quests.opening: We found a real service. Now we've found it twice on the same day's bill. One honest line doesn't excuse the second.
clues: Both invoices cover the same interval.
The nested line references the already settled container charge.
No additional berth or handling event appears in the log.
quests.answer: The duplicate interval, not the empty crate, proves the double charge.
choices: Refund the duplicate charge
The creditor loses claimed revenue
The corrected account preserves the original service fee.
Credit the buyer's next storage booking
Relief depends on using the port again
The account carries a compensating credit.
Place the duplicate sum in neutral escrow
Both sides wait for review
Neither party can spend the disputed amount yet.
quests.completion: Nothing was missing from the crate. Something was added to the bill.
quests.reward_lore: A ledger divider used to separate one service from two charges.

quests.title: A Port Without This Lie
quests.premise: A corrected claim can become a public precedent, a private settlement, or a monitored trial. Each protects different people.
quests.opening: A scandal sells faster than a standard. Tell me which one will still help the next dockhand.
clues: The storage unit is valid.
The reversed label explains the crate's journey.
The overlapping invoice interval proves the specific error.
quests.answer: A narrow, evidenced finding protects legitimate trade while correcting this duplicate charge.
choices: Publish an anonymized precedent
The buyer's personal story stays absent
The berth displays a general billing correction.
Negotiate a private settlement
Future buyers lack a public precedent
The parties settle without revealing their identities.
Run a jointly monitored billing trial
Workers must keep an extra record
Meridian and OmniCorp participants compare a limited test.
quests.completion: No secret empire behind this crate. Just a small lie large enough to ruin a worker. Small was worth your time.
quests.reward_lore: A signet bearing an empty crate. Earned by correcting a claim without condemning everyone who trades.

arcs.name: The Quiet Resonator
arcs.voice: We heard it. We haven't explained it.
arcs.motivation: Iren wants a witness willing to compare Arcanum measurements with Children of the Shard oral accounts without appropriating either or declaring the Shard conscious.
arcs.era: Present-day study of surviving infrastructure. A repeated sound cannot establish Shard sentience or reverse the Great Severance.
arcs.site: Three resonant ribs surround a fourth rib wrapped in old cloth. A listening bench faces away from the visible crystals toward a drainage channel.
arcs.monster_lore: A displaced rift beast nests in the gallery's maintenance channel. Its presence disrupts a physical test; it is not a messenger or personification of the Shard.

quests.title: Cloth on a Singing Rib
quests.premise: A cloth-wrapped rib sounds different from its neighbors. Iren asks whether deliberate damping was care, damage, or concealment.
quests.opening: Someone softened this note. Before we call it vandalism or a miracle, let's hear what they changed.
clues: Cloth touches the fourth rib at a vibration point.
The trace records lower amplitude, not a new word.
The cloth's wear suggests repeated maintenance.
quests.answer: The wrapping dampens vibration. The observation alone cannot explain the caretaker's belief or intent.
choices: Keep the damping while measuring
The unwrapped tone remains untested
The caretaker's intervention stays intact.
Remove it briefly with consent
The louder tone may disturb visitors
A limited comparison is recorded.
Make a nonintrusive external trace
The result has more uncertainty
The study avoids changing the rib.
quests.completion: A quieter note is a finding. Its meaning can remain a question.
quests.reward_lore: A fork tuned to a damped rib. Its tone is an observation, not a divine translation.

quests.title: The Bench Facing the Wrong Way
quests.premise: A listening bench faces a drain instead of the crystals. Its placement suggests the apparent reply has a second path.
quests.opening: The view is terrible. The listening position is excellent. Whoever sat here knew the difference.
clues: The bench faces the drainage channel.
A delayed note is loudest near its opening.
The rib-facing seat receives the first note but not the delay clearly.
quests.answer: The channel carries a delayed reflection; hearing a reply does not establish another speaker.

A cherished interpretation may be challenged
Visitors can compare both listening positions.
Discuss it with the oral custodians first
Public correction waits
The explanation begins with the people who preserve the account.
Publish the measurement without a verdict
Readers may still overinterpret it
The record separates timing from claims about a voice.
quests.completion: The second sound is real. A second speaker is still unproven.
quests.reward_lore: A token showing a bench turned away from spectacle and toward the sound's actual path.

quests.title: One Test Without a Witnessed Monster
quests.premise: A rift beast blocks the listening channel. Iren needs a safe test environment, not a ritual victory.
quests.opening: It's defending a nest. That doesn't make it a prophet. Clear the unsafe channel; don't write a revelation into the claws.
clues: Claw marks reach nesting debris in the channel.
The interference follows movement, not the rib's note.
The undisturbed trace still shows a reflection delay.
quests.answer: The beast causes intermittent interference; the measured reflection has a separate physical path.

The study collects fewer samples
The gallery receives a bounded test schedule.
Move observers to the outer bench
Measurements become less precise
The risky channel no longer hosts visitors.
Suspend invasive testing
The cause remains less fully characterized
Iren keeps the known result without expanding the disturbance.
quests.completion: Safe enough to listen. Not licensed to disturb everything that lives here.
quests.reward_lore: A boundary cord from a limited field test. A useful result need not justify unlimited intrusion.

quests.title: The Same Pause Twice
quests.premise: Two supposed prophetic replies share the same drainage interval. Iren can explain the repetition without adjudicating anyone's faith.
quests.opening: Two answers, one delay. The instrument measures the delay. It doesn't get to measure someone's faith.
clues: Both records use the same listening position.
Their delay matches the channel interval.
The claimed messages vary, while the recorded waveform repeats.
quests.answer: The measured repetition fits channel acoustics. This test cannot establish or disprove broader beliefs about Aethel.
choices: Publish a narrow acoustic finding
Dramatic claims remain outside its scope
The record corrects only what was measured.
Co-author the explanation with custodians
Agreement takes time
Observation and oral interpretation are attributed separately.
Archive raw traces for later review
The public gets no quick conclusion

quests.completion: We can be precise without pretending to be final.
quests.reward_lore: A crystal carrying two measured intervals. Similarity is evidence; intention is not established.

quests.title: The Silence Worth Keeping
quests.premise: The gallery can become a public experiment, a conserved listening place, or a jointly stewarded archive. Iren asks who may decide its next use.
quests.opening: I came for a complete explanation. I can leave with a careful one. Who should hold the next permission slip?
clues: The cloth is a physical intervention.
The bench reveals a reflection path.
The repeated interval supports a limited finding, not an account of Shard intention.
quests.answer: Stewardship can preserve both evidence and local consent without declaring one institution owner of the gallery's meaning.
choices: Conserve it as a listening place
New experiments become exceptional
The bench and wrapping remain undisturbed.
Permit supervised public comparisons
Custodians must manage visitor pressure
Visitors may hear the measured effect for themselves.
Create a jointly governed evidence archive
Neither group has unilateral authority
The traces remain available under shared permission.
quests.completion: It is still beautiful. Knowing one reason why doesn't take that away.
quests.reward_lore: A pendant engraved with a measured pause. It honors the limits of a finding, not mastery of the Shard.

arcs.name: The Unwritten Witness
arcs.voice: A finding has a boundary. Write it down.
arcs.motivation: Maela holds a limited mandate to compare a recent neutral relief archive with scattered field copies. She needs a witness outside its Custodian and AMA sponsors because both have an interest in appearing blameless.
arcs.era: A recent relief ceasefire archive housed in a surviving chamber. The archive is modern; the chamber is old. Neither proves a new cause of the Great Severance.
arcs.site: New lock bolts hold an old stone cabinet shut. A scorched relief ledger sits beside an undamaged metal duplicate, both bearing the same modern custody mark.
arcs.monster_lore: A drakonid displaced from the surrounding Shattered Heart has scorched a modern archive chamber. Its nesting explains local heat damage, not the Great Severance or a Custodian conspiracy.

quests.title: A Modern Lock on Ancient Stone
quests.premise: A modern custody lock conceals a relief archive inside an ancient chamber. Maela needs the two histories separated before rumors combine them.
quests.opening: The chamber is old. The lock is not. Please don't turn a relief office into the missing chapter of the Severance.
clues: The lock uses a current custody mark.
The ledger names a recent relief interval.
Ancient stone wear continues beneath fresh bolt heads.
quests.answer: A modern relief archive reuses an ancient chamber; its contents cannot date the chamber's original purpose.

The chamber's past remains unexplored

Request separate archaeological review
Review delays a complete site account
A second inquiry examines the stone without conflating it with the ledger.
quests.completion: Two histories can share a wall without becoming the same history.
quests.reward_lore: A modern seal from an old chamber. Its custody date is not the chamber's age.

quests.title: A Burn Without a Verdict
quests.premise: Heat damage resembles deliberate destruction, but its pattern could come from a displaced beast nesting beside the cabinet.
quests.opening: A damaged ledger is evidence of damage. Motive needs another page.
clues: Scorching is strongest beside the nesting recess.
The duplicate plate survives across the chamber.
The custody mark is unchanged on both versions.
quests.answer: The pattern supports localized heat exposure. It does not by itself establish intentional suppression.

Readers may still demand an immediate culprit

quests.completion: Uncertainty is not an acquittal. It is also not permission to invent a conviction.
quests.reward_lore: A plate tracing the limit of heat damage. It records a pattern, not an accusation.

quests.title: Safe Enough to Make a Copy
quests.premise: The nesting drakonid threatens anyone copying the relief records. Maela needs a safe chamber before commissioning an audit.
quests.opening: A dead archivist can't testify. Clear the immediate threat; we'll keep the report about what you actually found.

The drakonid has no custody token or institutional mark.
The duplicate survives independently of the damaged page.
quests.answer: Removing a present threat enables copying. It neither authenticates every entry nor proves who damaged the ledger earlier.

quests.completion: Now a second person can check the first person's work. That is a better safeguard than my reputation.
quests.reward_lore: A clip used to keep two independently witnessed archive copies together.

quests.title: The Reserve That Wasn't a Ransom
quests.premise: A line called withheld reserve looks like relief money seized as leverage. The duplicate identifies an unsettled payment, while leaving the delay's human cost visible.
quests.opening: AMA's wording is exact. A hungry household doesn't eat exact wording. Verify the reserve and keep the delay in the finding.
clues: The reserve line names an unsettled transfer.
The duplicate has a release condition but no faction-concession clause.
A field note records recipients waiting while settlement was checked.
quests.answer: The documented reserve is pending settlement, not proven ransom. That does not make the relief delay harmless or automatically justified.
choices: Publish both the settlement reason and delay
Sponsors face criticism despite a valid accounting category
The record preserves the cost borne by recipients.
Request an emergency relief exception
The authority must accept additional settlement risk
A narrow exception request accompanies the audited account.
Seek independent review of the hold
Release may be further delayed
A neutral review tests whether the hold was proportionate.
quests.completion: A precise account can still describe a failure of care. Keep both sentences.
quests.reward_lore: An audit countertoken identifying a reserve without pretending the people waiting for it suffered no cost.

quests.title: The Unwritten Witness
quests.premise: Records from the ward, yard, berth, gallery, and vault show how institutions can mistake absence, silence, or delay for consent. Maela offers no revelation about a hidden ruler, only a decision about who may challenge the archive.
quests.opening: Five places. Five ways a neat record can injure someone. I can't award you the truth about Xylos. I can ask who gets to correct this shelf after us.
clues: The ward separates recognition from disclosure; the yard separates absence from desertion.
The berth separates a valid unit from a duplicate charge; the gallery separates sound from intention.
The vault separates accounting accuracy from the consequences of delay.
quests.answer: The common failure is treating a record as permission to stop listening. An appeal mechanism preserves correction without making every disputed account equally true.
choices: Create a public, redacted appeal index
Transparency needs careful privacy work
People can challenge entries without revealing protected identities.
Establish distributed local custodians
Corrections are slower to reconcile
Each site keeps a voice in its own record.
Create a rotating independent review
Reviewers require resources and can still err

quests.completion: Your name goes on the witness line, not the ownership line. Leave room beneath it for the person who proves us wrong.
quests.reward_lore: Five grooves surround an unfinished witness line. The final groove remains open for a correction not yet heard.
